acme/tinycsv.author: lee
acme/tinycsv.title: Support a custom delimiter in read_rows
acme/tinycsv.body:
read_rows always splits on commas. Add a `delimiter` argument (default ',') so tab- and semicolon-separated files work.

Steps: call read_rows(text, delimiter=';').
Expected: rows split on semicolons.
The parser lives in tinycsv/__init__.py.

comments.author: maria
comments.body: Happy to review a PR for this. Keep the default unchanged.

acme/tinycsv.author: lee
acme/tinycsv.title: Add type hints to the public API
acme/tinycsv.body: Functions in tinycsv/__init__.py have no type hints.

acme/tinycsv.author: kim
acme/tinycsv.title: Handle a UTF-8 BOM at the start of the file
acme/tinycsv.body: Files exported from Excel start with a BOM and the first header gets mangled.

acme/tinycsv.author: kim
acme/tinycsv.title: Document the quoting rules
acme/tinycsv.body: The README does not explain how quotes inside fields are handled.

comments.author: sam
comments.body: I'd like to work on this, can you assign me?

acme/tinycsv.author: lee
acme/tinycsv.title: write_rows should quote fields that contain newlines
acme/tinycsv.body:
write_rows([['a\nb']]) produces a broken file. Fields with newlines must be quoted.

Expected: "a\nb" in quotes. See tinycsv/__init__.py write_rows.

comments.author: maria
comments.body: Confirmed, a test case would be great too.

acme/dateparse.author: ana
acme/dateparse.title: Parse ISO week dates like 2024-W05-3
acme/dateparse.body: parse('2024-W05-3') should return the Wednesday of ISO week 5. The parser is in dateparse/__init__.py; add a regex branch for week dates and tests.

comments.author: ivo
comments.body: Yes please, ISO 8601 week dates are in scope.

acme/dateparse.author: ana
acme/dateparse.title: Refactor the timezone handling
acme/dateparse.body: Timezone handling is spread across several modules and should be unified. This is a large change touching most of the package; needs a design first.

comments.author: ivo
comments.body: Agreed, let's discuss a design in this issue first.
